summary.en: Militant gunmen continue to target police protecting polio vaccination teams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killing two officers and wounding another in Mohmand, while a separate attack in Karachi killed a PIA engineer. Border clashes intensified as Pakistani forces returned fire on Afghan Taliban posts in South Waziristan after Taliban fire on Pakistani posts. Economic pressure is rising, with LPG prices surging and threatening poor commuters. Iran is planning a four-party meeting on Afghanistan in the coming months. The conflict caused 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantvåpnede menn fortsetter å angripe politiet som beskytter poliovaksinasjonsteam i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, og drepte to offiserer og såret en annen i Mohmand, mens et separat angrep i Karachi drepte en PIA-ingeniør. Grensekonfliktene intensiverte da pakistanske styrker svarte med ild på afghanske Taliban-poster i Sør-Waziristan etter at Taliban skjøt på pakistanske poster. Det økonomiske presset øker, med LPG-priser som skyter i været og truer fattige pendlere. Iran planlegger et firepartimøte om Afghanistan i de kommende månedene. Konflikten forårsaket 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
